content.text:
I have now inspected every responsive location. Summary of the bargain:

- **§ 6.0 SOW (p0720)** — "MSL agrees to produce and sell, and IBM agrees to purchase Products. **This Agreement does not authorize MSL to produce or deliver any Product.**" No quantity, no minimum.
- **§ 11.2(d) (p0882)** — forecasts "do not obligate IBM to purchase any Product."
- **§ 1.8 (p0065) / § 11.2 (p0870)** — only IBM Customer Orders/Purchase Orders authorize build; Products produced "according to actual intake of IBM Customer Orders."
- **§ 6.1 (p0722)** — IBM may cancel any and all Purchase Orders at any time (exit).
- **§ 13.2(e) (p0927)** — "IBM will have no liability for unused flexibility"; **§ 13.0(f) (p0903)** — no liability for MSL-purchased inventory within forecast-accuracy parameters; **§ 13.3(b)** — untransferred EOL inventory is MSL's sole responsibility.
- Residual exposure is cost-reimbursement only: Appendix 2 Requirements Accuracy compensation and § 5.2/5.3 termination buyout of non-cancellable Parts **at MSL's cost** — a true-up, not a shortfall penalty.

No minimum purchase or volume commitment exists, so no redline is warranted.

input.quote: d) The forecasts provided by IBM, or agreed to by IBM hereunder, do not obligate IBM to purchase any Product.
input.rationale: There is no minimum purchase, volume or take-or-pay commitment on IBM anywhere in the Base Agreement, Statement of Work or Appendices. SOW § 11.2(d) states forecasts "do not obligate IBM to purchase any Product"; SOW § 6.0 says the Agreement "does not authorize MSL to produce or deliver any Product"; and § 1.8 provides that only IBM Customer Orders or an IBM Purchase Order authorize MSL to build, so IBM pays only for Products it actually orders (price formula at § 7.1). IBM also retains an exit: § 6.1 lets IBM "cancel any and all Purchase Orders against this Agreement at any time." That places the deal at (indeed above) the preferred position; the fallback 12-month/30-day reduction machinery is inapplicable because no commitment exists to limit or reduce. The residual exposures flagged in review are cost true-ups, not shortfall penalties, and are bounded in IBM's favour: on termination IBM buys only non-cancellable Parts at "an amount equal to MSL's cost" (§ 5.3(b)); IBM "has no liability for inventories that MSL purchases" within the forecast-accuracy parameters (§ 13.0(f)); and "IBM will have no liability for unused flexibility" (§ 13.2(e)), with Appendix 4 Supply Flexibility being an MSL upside obligation that benefits us. The Appendix 2 Requirements Accuracy compensation is a materials-cost true-up on IBM's own forecast rather than a purchase minimum; it is a sub-preferred wrinkle worth noting commercially (the percentages are redacted) but not a fallback failure, and we do not redline it.
